To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NoC architectures can be evaluated using an analytical methodology that provides a good approximation to actual system performance.

(i) the performance of NoC architectures depends on the traffic pattern and the number of cores; (ii) the performance of the NoC architecture is not sensitive to the number of routers; (iii) NoC architectures that have a high degree of regularity, such as the fat tree and the mesh, are more energy efficient; and (iv) for a given NoC architecture, the performance is not very sensitive to the number and type of buffers in the network.

(1) the mesh topology provides the best performance and scalability, (2) the mesh with a wormhole routing protocol is the most energy-efficient, and (3) the mesh with an XY routing protocol is the best in terms of area efficiency.

the design of communication-centric interconnect architectures for MP-SoC, and our main contributions are the following: (1) a consistent evaluation methodology for NoC architectures; (2) a set of comparative results for a variety of NoCs; and (3) a case study of a typical MP-SoC platform mapped to different NoCs.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the network-on-chip (or NoC) approach is a viable solution to the problem of interconnect design for multiprocessor system-on-a-chip (MPSoC) platforms.

the NoC approach is a promising alternative to traditional bus architectures for MP-SoC designs, and that it offers many design trade-offs that can be exploited by designers to meet their performance and energy requirements.
the performance and design trade-off analysis of NoC architectures can be used as a guideline for the design of future MP-SoC architectures.
